statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 19%, inside the low band, while Stress at 56% remains the elevated reading.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON on Tail 19%. The elevated component is Stress at 56%, carried by a ten-year near two-decade highs, roughly 73% odds on an October Fed hike and crude still above $90, rather than by observed Nasdaq-100 trend persistence. The narrow danger window runs from the 18:00Z Fed Hammack appearance to the 21:00Z CME weekly futures halt, covering the power hour and Friday position-squaring. Beyond 21:00Z the remainder of the horizon is halted time in which no mean-reversion failure can develop.
headline: Session low beneath Thursday's close fully bought back with VIX at 15 and yields off their peak; two-way tape holds Tail in the low band
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades 30,639.91, up 0.53% against a 30,478.86 previous close, inside a 30,413.59 to 30,667.56 session range. The structural point is that both directions have been paid: the session low broke beneath Thursday's close and was recovered in full, roughly 226 points, while the marginal high has not been held, with price some 28 points below it. That is retracement working in both directions rather than the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension signature that would justify a higher Tail. Volatility is decaying alongside it, VIX 15.02 and down 4.15% near its 14.86 session low. Cross-assets describe relief inside a stressed regime. The ten-year is 5.19%, up 3 basis points but off a 5.23% intraday high, after a three-session selloff that carried it to its highest since 2007 and the thirty-year to levels last seen in 2004. WTI is $92.13, down 2.62%, on reports of US-Iran negotiations over a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz at the UN General Assembly sidelines. Semiconductors lead, SOX +1.69% at 12,704.01 without trading beneath Thursday's close, though Nvidia is only +0.20%, so the leadership is broad rather than megacap-concentrated. Today's data cut both ways. August durable goods printed 0.0% against a -0.4% consensus with core capital-goods orders +1.6% versus +0.5% expected, while the final September Michigan sentiment fell to 48.1, a four-month low, and one-year inflation expectations jumped to 4.6% from 4.0%. Futures now price roughly 73% odds of a hike at the October 27-28 FOMC. That combination is a genuinely difficult environment and is what the elevated Stress reading measures. It is not, on current evidence, a pathological price path: Tail stays in the low band. The dominant feature of the forward horizon is mechanical, namely the CME weekly futures halt at 21:00Z, after which twenty of the twenty-four published slots are untradeable time.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours stayed inside a narrow band: Tail between 17% and 22%, Stress between 54% and 59%, and Confidence between 86% and 88%, alternating between EA_ON and WATCH without approaching the block threshold at any point. Dominant mode ran mixed through the US afternoon and evening, normal across the 01:00Z to 05:00Z Asian hours, then produced four trend-up readings during the European morning and the US pre-market before reverting to mixed. The 13:00Z slot has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable with null assessment fields. The last two published hours eased back to 19% and 18% Tail, which is the reading the current assessment continues.
outlookSummary: The near-term path keeps Tail inside the low and watch bands, rising to 21% across the 18:00Z Fed Hammack appearance and the power hour into the Friday cash close, which together define the narrow danger window. The defining feature of this horizon is the CME weekly futures halt at 21:00Z: the last twenty hourly slots are halted, untradeable time in which no mean-reversion failure can develop, so Tail falls to a 10% then 9% residual and the published action returns to EA_ON throughout. Stress holds in the elevated band because the rates and energy backdrop is carried forward rather than resolved, and Confidence decays steadily from 86% to 55% to label an assessment that cannot be refreshed while every relevant venue is closed. The Sunday reopen, and with it the weekend gap risk from the unresolved Hormuz negotiation, falls outside this window.

VIX 15.02 (-4.15%), the 10-year 5.19% off its 5.23% peak, WTI $92.13 (-2.62%). Both directions paid, so Tail holds the low band.
